transcript.text: Norns, I am here. Speak, tell me what my fate holds. What troubles you?

transcript.speaker: antagonist

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I know. I feel it. But what does this mean? Am I doomed?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Doomed? Fate is not so simple as a single thread snapping. But your thread is weakened where it should be strongest. To fight now, to call upon the storm... it risks unraveling you entirely. You must step back from the fray. For a full turn of the moon, at least.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: One month?

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *(She finally looks up, her eyes like deep wells reflecting no light)* One cycle of the moon. To let the weave settle. To see if the poison fades... or festers. I cannot promise you will ever lift your hammer with the same ease again. The threads are unclear.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, Norns, for your wisdom. I shall hearken to your words and trust that they guide me. My path is not yet decided, but I will make the best of it. Thank you for sharing this knowledge with me. I am grateful.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *(She gives a slow, solemn nod, her hands stilling over the threads)* Your gratitude is a rare thread in itself, Thor Odinson. Go in peace. Watch the moon. We will watch the weave.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *He turns and strides away from the Norns, his steps heavy and his heart troubled. He knows their warning holds truth.*
